pull.title: Kernel blockstorage pruning
pull.body:
I would like to be able to do pruning in the kernel-node, but right now the kernel can't open a data directory that Bitcoin Core has pruned or prune its own block storage. 

This separates block storage from chainstate management first and then adds pruning to the kernel API.

Commits 1 to 6 are refactors, and should not impose any behavior change. Commits 7 to 10 add a block manager and pruning to the kernel API

1. Apply prune locks in BlockManager instead of in validation.
2. Give BlockManager a height range and sizes to prune within, instead of letting it read the chainstate.
3. Move ImportBlocks, which drives validation, out of block storage.
4. Remove the friend declarations, so validation only uses BlockManager's public interface.
5. Create the BlockManager first and pass it to ChainstateManager by reference. Block storage then no longer belongs to chainstate management.
6. Remove ChainstateLoadOptions::prune, which duplicated BlockManager's prune mode.
7. Add `btck_BlockManager` and read blocks through it. This changes the first parameter of `btck_block_read` and `btck_block_spent_outputs_read`.
8. Add pruning up to a height and prune locks. Also lets the kernel open a data directory that Bitcoin Core has pruned.
9. Add automatic pruning to a target size.
10. Add `btck_chainstate_manager_get_first_available_entry`

kernel: add pruning

Add an option to enable pruning, and block manager functions to prune up
to a height and to set and delete prune locks. The option also lets the
kernel open a data directory that Bitcoin Core has pruned.

Pruning still goes through the active chainstate, which decides what may
be deleted.

Export a fast prune setter only for test_kernel, since test chains never
fill a 128 MiB block file.

kernel: add automatic pruning

Add a target size option. Blocks are then deleted to stay below it,
except the 288 most recent and those kept by prune locks. Prune locks
can also be set in the options, because loading can already trigger
pruning.

Automatic deletion is untested, as test chains never reach the 550 MiB
minimum target.

kernel: expose first available block tree entry

Return the lowest active chain entry from which every block up to the
tip can be read with its spent outputs. Spent outputs count because a
pruned block that is processed again is stored without them.

Move GetPruneHeight from rpc to node/blockstorage so the kernel can use
it. Review with --color-moved.

### LLM Linter (✨ experimental)



Possible typos and grammar issues:

- `// make sure we don't prune above any of the prune locks bestblocks` -> `// make sure we don't prune above any of the prune locks' best blocks` [“bestblocks” is a typo; the intended phrase is unclear without splitting it into two words]




Possible places where comparison-specific test macros should replace generic comparisons:

- [src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp] `BOOST_CHECK_THROW(chain.GetByHeight(1000), std::runtime_error);` -> Prefer `BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION` with a predicate that checks the exception text, rather than only the generic exception type.
- [src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp] `BOOST_CHECK_THROW(blockman.ReadBlockSpentOutputs(chain.GetByHeight(1)), std::runtime_error);` -> Prefer `BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION` with a message matcher to validate the specific failure.
- [src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp] `BOOST_CHECK_THROW(create_chainman(test_directory, /*reindex=*/false, /*wipe_chainstate=*/false, /*block_tree_db_in_memory=*/false, /*chainstate_db_in_memory=*/false, context), std::runtime_error);` -> Prefer `BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION` with a predicate on the error message.
- [src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp] `BOOST_CHECK_THROW(blockman.ReadBlockSpentOutputs(tip), std::runtime_error);` -> Prefer `BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION` with a message matcher instead of only asserting the exception type.
